title: Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions

issues.location: Sec. 4, Prop. 4.1 (two-intercept reshaping), together with the companion surface paper
issues.description: This is a note on how strong the claim is, not a demonstrated gap. The planar reshaping machinery (node valuation nu_t, shear, coordinate compressions, primitive direction) also runs for n=2. Starting from Delta(1,1) on P^2 it reaches Delta(1/sqrt r, sqrt r), which would prove Nagata's conjecture for P^2 at large r. Even outside the paper's dw<1/16 regime, the choice u=(1,1) with t of about 16.5 seems to give r=10. A result of that size calls for independent expert checking of the jet-transfer-by-degeneration steps (Lemmas 2.4, 2.5 and 2.7 and the node step), even though I found no error in them.
issues.evidence: From P=conv{(-b,0),(a,0),(0,1/3)} with a in (2.7,3): u=(1,1) gives range R=a+1/3, and a=sqrt(10)-1/3=2.829 is admissible (t=a/(3-a) is about 16.5, above T=9). I checked consistency with the known non-maximal cases r<=8: under every operation min(A,B) cannot increase (plain lattice moves give R in {A,B} or R>=max(A,B); a node move gives R>=a>(6/7)W>=1.7/min(A,B)). So no shape reachable from Delta(1,1) beats the known values for r=2,3,5,6,7,8. A breadth-first search over reachable shapes, started as a numerical cross-check, was stopped before it finished; this conclusion rests on the analytic argument.

coverage:
I read all of main.tex: introduction, transfers, flag, reshaping, saturation and conclusion. I did not audit the companion surface paper beyond the fact that it is not used as an input. Steps checked by hand:
- Least-term and row-valuation lemmas.
- Weighted-limit and rank-persistence lemmas.
- Unimodular and coordinate-compression lemmas, including the row bound and the Laurent case.
- The flag simplex bound.
- The node exponent bound, the envelope Q, area(Q)=H/2, and convexity for t>T.
- The shear and compression slice computations, giving P=conv{(-b,0),(a,0),(0,c)}.
- The primitive-direction choice: j>4, an interval of length >2, an odd i, a in (a0,W), and range R.
- The tent and final compressions to Delta(w,R).
- The iteration hypotheses (A,B>=ell, product V).
- Interior saturation.
- Hermite interpolation on E_{r,m} inside k*lambda*P.
- The Baire-category argument for a very-general locus.
- The jets-to-curves lemma (Hilbert–Samuel) and the volume upper bound.

Numerical check: for P^2 with t=10 and k=3,5,7, I computed nu_t of the full space of degree-<=k polynomials in node coordinates by elimination mod p. The counts match C(k+2,2), every least exponent lies in kQ, and the sets fill the lattice points of kQ exactly.
main_claim: For smooth projective X of dimension n>=3 and ample L, there is r0 such that for every r>=r0 the multipoint Seshadri constant at r very general points equals (L^n/r)^{1/n}.
sibling_notes: When I checked, the hive board for family 039 had no earlier entries. The paper says it does not use the companion surfaces paper (OpenAI2026Surfaces) as an input, and it re-proves the node, compression and primitive-direction steps itself. Siblings auditing the surface paper should note that the same planar argument implies Nagata for P^2, so its node and jet-transfer steps deserve the closest scrutiny.
